content.text:
I've submitted **index 2** (Bi 0.22, Cu 0.30, V 0.48) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured: **44.7 µA**. All 3 merit measurements and all 5 XRD measurements are used.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent | Phases seen by XRD |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 | 1.24 µA | BiVO4 |
| **2** | **0.22 / 0.30 / 0.48** | **44.7 µA** | BiVO4 plus a second phase (peak at Q 1.746) |
| 4 | 0.18 / 0.34 / 0.48 | 37.3 µA | Same as index 2 |

- **What worked:** index 2, with some Cu added, gave about 36 times more photocurrent than index 7, the Cu-poor BiVO4 composition. The second phase is probably a copper vanadate, but I never matched it to a simulated pattern, so that's a guess. Index 4 kept the same phases but gave less current, so the best point is probably close to index 2.
- **Not measured:** at index 41 (Bi 0.14, Cu 0.40, V 0.46) XRD showed the Q 1.746 phase replaced by a different one. Index 12, a Bi-rich composition, was a mix of many phases. I didn't spend a measurement on either.
- **The model checks told me little:** the phase list was too long to display and I had no way to read the file it was saved to, so I found valid structure IDs by guessing. The only ones that worked were four simple binary oxides: Cu2O, V2O5, CuO and Bi2O3. The required checks therefore rest on their band gaps, not on BiVO4 or any copper vanadate. My choices came mainly from prior knowledge that BiVO4 is a good photoanode, from the XRD patterns, and from the measured trend.

With only three measurements, other compositions near index 2 (such as 5, 6 or 9) could do better; none of them were measured.
